title: Bypassing the Decoupled Adapter (The Leaky Framework Base)
pattern: Directly subclassing, embedding, or inheriting database framework base classes inside core domain entity structures.
why_bad: It leaks the third-party framework's entire API into the business domain. Downstream callers bypass domain rules by calling framework methods directly, making future upgrades or migrations to other persistence backends extremely expensive and labor-intensive [774].
detection: Domain-level types declaring public fields or traits that are explicitly owned by a third-party framework (e.g., ORM models, web framework request handlers).
counterexample: Valid for rapid prototypes or low-scale Transaction Scripts where domain separation is not prioritized.
